sections.title: A Distinguished Education in One of Europe’s Most Dynamic Countries
sections.intro: Spain combines internationally respected universities and business schools with an outstanding quality of life and costs that compare favourably with other global study hubs.

items.title: Europe-wide recognition
items.desc: Degrees follow the European Higher Education Area framework, supporting recognition and mobility across Europe.

items.title: Academic strengths
items.desc: Spain’s universities and business schools are world-renowned in business, engineering, architecture, design, health sciences, tourism and social sciences.

items.title: A global language
items.desc: Mastery of Spanish opens professional career horizons across Europe, Latin America and global international organizations.

items.title: Practical career pathways
items.desc: University students on a student visa may work up to 30 hours per week, and eligible graduates can explore stay-back permits to work.

items.title: An exceptional lifestyle
items.desc: From Madrid to Barcelona and Valencia, student life is vibrant, sociable, safe and outdoors-oriented with a pleasant Mediterranean climate.

sections.intro: The following institutions represent key destinations available to EUROPA FUSION students.

items.name: Complutense University of Madrid
items.desc: One of Spain’s largest and oldest universities, offering an exceptionally broad range of programmes in humanities, sciences, law and health.

items.name: Autonomous University of Madrid
items.desc: A premier research-led university widely respected for sciences, medicine, economics, biotechnology and the humanities.

items.name: Carlos III University of Madrid
items.desc: Known for law, social sciences, business, economics and engineering, with a strongly international and employment-focused profile.

items.name: University of Barcelona
items.desc: A comprehensive research university with notable strengths in health sciences, humanities, life sciences, economics and the arts.

items.name: Pompeu Fabra University
items.desc: A top-ranked modern institution distinguished for economics, political science, communication, law and data science.

items.name: Polytechnic University of Valencia
items.desc: A leading destination for engineering, computer science, architecture, design and applied technology, with close industry links.

items.name: IE University
items.desc: An internationally oriented private university and business school focused on business, technology, law, leadership and innovation.

items.name: ESADE Business School
items.desc: Internationally recognized for management, business administration and law programmes, with a global alumni and corporate network.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.intro: Common questions about studying and settling in Spain.

items.q: Can I study in Spain entirely in English?
items.a: Yes. Spain offers a wide choice of English-taught programmes, particularly at Master’s level and at private universities and business schools. Many public Bachelor’s programmes are taught in Spanish, so the language of instruction should be confirmed for each course.

items.q: Do I need to speak Spanish?
items.a: It is not required for English-taught programmes, but Spanish greatly enhances daily life, part-time work and career prospects. For Spanish-taught degrees, certified proficiency (such as DELE or SIELE B2) is requested.

items.q: How much does it cost to study in Spain?
items.a: Public university tuition is set by each regional autonomous community and charged per credit (€700 to €2,500/yr for Bachelor’s; €1,000 to €5,000/yr for Master’s). Private universities charge €6,000 to €20,000+. Living costs commonly range from €800 to €1,400 per month.

items.q: When are the intakes and deadlines?
items.a: The main intake begins in September or October, with a smaller number of programmes starting in February. Application windows at public universities typically fall in the spring and early summer (April–June). Early preparation is advisable.
Most English-taught programmes request IELTS (typically 6.0–7.0), TOEFL, or equivalent tests.

items.q: How much money must I show for the student visa?
items.a: Applicants must demonstrate sufficient funds benchmarked at 100% of the IPREM (approx. €600 per month, or €7,200 for a twelve-month stay), excluding tuition fees.

items.q: Can I work while studying in Spain?
items.a: University students holding a student visa in Spain may generally work up to 30 hours per week, provided the employment is compatible with study hours.

items.q: Can I remain in Spain after graduating?
items.a: Yes. Graduates may apply for a 1-year residence permit to look for employment or launch a business startup, or modify their status directly to an employment contract or EU Blue Card.

items.q: Are scholarships available for international students?
items.a: Yes. Spanish universities, regional governments, and private foundations offer merit and need-based tuition waivers, while Erasmus Mundus provides full scholarships for selected Master’s degrees.
Options include Colegios Mayores (university residences), shared flats (*pisos compartidos*), and private purpose-built student housing across Madrid, Barcelona, and Valencia.

Typically: passport, academic transcripts and degrees (apostilled & translated), language certificate, CV, motivation letter, medical certificate, police clearance certificate, and proof of €7,200+ IPREM funds.

items.q: How does EUROPA FUSION support my application?
items.a: We handle profile evaluation, UNEDasiss accreditation guidance, document legalization/sworn translations, university applications, Spanish visa file processing, and housing search.
